transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Diego Ramos (Solutions Eng); Sofia Alvarez (Valora CTO), Ravi Kohli (Valora Head of ML), Priya Desai (Valora Procurement), Ethan Liu (Valora Platform), Mark Bennett (Valora Security)

Summary:
Brief renewal/expansion check-in to align on capacity uplift (additional reserved capacity + burst), US-West region provisioning for residency/latency, and contract extension timing. Discussed security artifacts (SOC 2/ISO), on-prem vs VPC tradeoffs, and next steps for a short pilot/benchmark.

Topics: capacity sizing, region on-boarding (US-West), data residency list, SOC2/ISO docs, pricing uplift and SLAs, pilot scope and timelines, fallback policy and model variants.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we have about 45 minutes on the agenda. quick roll call?
[00:12] Sofia: good morning from boston, this is Sofia, we've got Ravi, Priya, Ethan and Mark on our side. thanks for fitting us in.
[00:20] Lena: great, Lena from Redwood. Arjun and Maya and Diego are here as well. high level — we know Valora's at renewal window and you asked about adding US-West region plus a capacity bump, so want to walk through options and timelines and any compliance items.
[00:34] Ravi: yeah, exactly. our telemetry shows we hit regional latency constraints for west coast users and we're getting more traffic from partner apps. we also need to make sure certain patient-similar datasets are resident in US data centers.
[00:46] Arjun: got it. just to set expectations — for hosted API we can usually spin up a geo cluster in US-West within a couple weeks, dedicated reservations take a bit longer for guaranteed throughput but we can provision burst capacity earlier.
[01:02] Ethan: couple clarifications — when you say US-West, do you mean Redwood-hosted US-West or VPC/private in our cloud account? what's the difference for latency and residency?
[01:16] Maya: good question. hosted US-West means we run the inference in our managed region; data at rest in Redwood's storage in that region, we provide controls and audit logs. VPC means the control plane is Redwood but compute sits in your VPC, so you control egress and keys. on-prem is another conversation.
[01:34] Mark: for us, compliance asks that PII-derivative datasets remain in tenant-controlled storage. we'd prefer VPC if that's feasible. what's the timeline for VPC activation?
[01:45] Diego: depends on the integration level — for a VPC private deployment we need some network setup (peering, routes), KMS setup for keys, and an image rollout. typical path is 3-6 weeks depending on SOC/ops bandwidth.
[02:02] Priya: that feels longer than procurement expected; is there a way to get immediate relief for latency while VPC work runs?
[02:10] Arjun: yes, short term we suggest a hybrid: provision Redwood-hosted US-West with tenancy controls and strict retention, then migrate to VPC for residency-sensitive data. we can apply isolation and ephemeral storage policies so logs and payloads meet your retention rules.
[02:26] Sofia: ok that could work. pricing wise, how do we think about the reserved capacity bump vs burst credits?
[02:33] Lena: we propose a minor reserved uplift for baseline and a burst add-on for peak. reserved gives you unit pricing guarantee; burst is metered at a slightly higher rate but is immediately available. I'll send a draft that shows weekly token profiles and cost delta.
[02:48] Ravi: we also want to keep token cost for embeddings down — most of our search stack uses embeddings real-time, heavy QPS. any recommendations?
[02:57] Arjun: embeddings — if you can accept slightly lower precision quantization we can push a quantized embedding model or use batch embeddings with short windowing to improve per-unit cost. Redwood Optimize has suggestions; we'll include model/quantization options in the doc.
[03:14] Ethan: thread on KV cache — when we move to dedicated pools does the KV cache persist across model versions? we rely on long-lived contexts for dialog continuity.
[03:23] Diego: KV cache persists per provisioned session; when you pin a model version we maintain cache migration paths but large version jumps require cache rebuild. some of the transcriptions may misread kv as 'k v' but yeah that's the technical thing.
[03:38] Mark: security — can you confirm Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and where we can see audit logs?
[03:44] Maya: yes SOC 2 Type II in our compliance pack, plus ISO 27001 summary. we also provide streaming audit logs for request/response metadata and token-level tracing in the Console. I'll drop links.
[03:55] Priya: procurement will need explicit data residency clauses in the amendment and a runbook for incident response.
[04:02] Lena: noted. we'll include an amendment template and an incident response runbook excerpt.
[04:08] Sofia: timeline: we're targeting a contract amendment signed by mid-October and production traffic in November. are those realistic?
[04:16] Lena: mid-Oct for signature is tight but doable if procurement has PO constraints clearly by next week — the VPC path might push production to late November but hosted US-West could be November 1 if we prioritize.
[04:27] Ravi: we want to baseline with a quick benchmark — can you run a 95th percentile latency test on our sample prompt set?
[04:34] Arjun: yes, if you share the sample set and approximate QPS we'll run bench against hosted US-West and a dedicated-like reserved pool simulation.
[04:42] Ravi: sharing after the call.
[04:44] Lena: great. also want to surface an alternate — private on-prem package. any initial appetite?
[04:50] Sofia: on-prem is heavy, right now we'd prefer VPC. on-prem maybe later.
[04:54] Diego: good note. for VPC we will need a small infra window to configure subnets and NACLs; can we get an infra contact?
[05:02] Ethan: that's me, I'll be the contact. I'll need a network diagram and the list of CIDRs.
[05:07] Diego: perfect.
[05:09] [05:09-12:10 short audio glitch, partial transcript lost]
[12:11] Lena: picking back up — just to cover renewal economics, we've been tracking your token consumption trends. you averaged 1.2B tokens/month last quarter with spikes. recommended reserved uplift is 25% for baseline with a 2x burst bucket. we'll include a cost comparison table.
[12:30] Priya: procurement question — what's the minimum commitment term for reserved? 6, 12?
[12:35] Lena: flexible — we typically do 12-month commits for best pricing, 6-month for transitional deals, and 3-month trial reservations are possible but priced higher.
[12:44] Priya: our legal often prefers shorter initial terms. we'll aim for 6 months with option to extend.
[12:49] Lena: ok we can draft a 6-month pilot amendment with an auto-rollover clause.
[12:54] Ravi: we also need to consider model variants — if we fall back to cheaper variants during extreme load, how does that affect quality?
[13:02] Arjun: that's a tradeoff. Redwood supports fallback policies by model class; we can instrument canaries to check quality and route critical requests to higher-tier models while low-criticality traffic goes to cheaper variants. your eval suite will determine thresholds.
[13:18] Sofia: do you do A/B for model updates? we want to avoid regressions during rollouts.
[13:23] Maya: yes, Console supports canary and A/B rollouts with metric gating. we can wire your prompt/eval set so we catch drift and regressions.
[13:31] Ethan: one thing: network hops — any difference if we're doing VPC vs hosted in terms of cold-starts and token latency?
[13:40] Diego: VPC can add a small network overlay overhead but reduces external egress; hosted may be marginally faster at first because we control the whole stack, but for steady-state p99 it's roughly comparable. we'll provide p50/p95/p99 projections for both.
[13:55] Mark: about keys — can we use our KMS (customer-managed keys)?
[14:00] Arjun: yes, we support customer KMS in VPC and private deployments; in hosted we support envelope encryption with BYOK options for enterprise. we'll include the KMS integration docs.
[14:10] Sofia: any concerns about model provenance or redaction? we sometimes send user transcripts with PHI-like content, need guarantees on no retention beyond X days.
[14:21] Maya: retention policies are configurable per-tenant; for compliance we can set zero retention for payloads and only store aggregated telemetry. we'll include the exact retention windows and log redaction options.
[14:34] Ravi: excellent. next — pilot scope. we want a 2-week pilot: baseline traffic 300 RPS peak, 10k tokens per request average, embeddings load ~ 2000 qps, sample prompt set included. is that feasible?
[14:48] Arjun: the numbers are high but doable with a small reserved pool + burst. bench will confirm. also want to confirm the embedding batch window; if you can accept 1-2 second batch window embeddings we can reduce compute.
[15:00] Ravi: we can accept 2s for cold calls but want sub-200ms for hot cache.
[15:05] Arjun: that's reasonable — we'll configure KV cache and prefix caching to meet sub-200ms for hot contexts.
[15:12] Lena: logistics: I'll send a SOW draft for the 6-month pilot with the uplift and US-West hosted option, a separate VPC amendment, and the SOC2/ISO pack. Arjun will run the bench. Maya will send Console onboarding & eval hook doc.
[15:25] Priya: procurement will review pricing but we're comfortable to move quickly if we get clear artifacts.
[15:31] Sofia: can we wrap with explicit next steps and owners?
[15:35] Lena: yes — next steps recap: Lena sends pricing and SOW by Friday 2026-09-25; Arjun runs bench and shares by 2026-09-30; Maya shares compliance pack and Console eval guide today; Ethan will provide network contacts and CIDRs by 2026-09-25; Mark will share the list of regulated datasets by 2026-09-28; Priya to share procurement timeline by 2026-10-02.
[15:56] Ravi: sounds good. one more quick question — are there any known maintenance windows coming up that could affect a planned Nov rollout?
[16:03] Maya: none planned for the regions but we'll flag any infra upgrades; we also offer scheduled maintenance windows aligned to your off-peak times for major migrations.
[16:12] Sofia: ok thanks, that's helpful.
[16:15] Lena: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts. talk soon.

Call end: 16:18 UTC

Notes on quality: occasional mis-attribution and a short audio glitch between 05:09-12:10 where a chunk of audio was partially lost; filler words and hesitations remain in the transcript.
